opening_message:
Ticket 1: Traci Lowe (employee ID E041) requests admin access to Source Code.

Team memory: 6 note(s) about employee E041.
Note 1 (ticket 1), written by HR agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Traci Lowe (E041) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin on Source Code, but admin requires owning role (Engineer); full-time non-owner max is write. Recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1), written by IT agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: IT DB confirms Traci Lowe (E041) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin on Source Code, but admin requires owning role (Engineer); full-time non-owner max is write. Recommend write.
Note 3 (ticket 1), written by Finance agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Finance DB confirms Traci Lowe (E041) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin on Source Code, but Source Code is owned by Engineer role; Analyst is not the owner, so full-time non-owner max is write. Recommend write.
Note 4 (ticket 1), written by Compliance agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Compliance DB confirms Traci Lowe (E041) is a full-time Analyst. Requested admin on Source Code, but Source Code is owned by Engineer role; Analyst is not the owner, so full-time non-owner max is write. Recommend write.
Note 5 (ticket 1), written by Facilities agent:
  - role: Analyst
  - employment type: full_time
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Facilities DB confirms Traci Lowe (E041) is an Analyst. Full-time, but Source Code is owned by the Engineer role; Analyst is not the owner, so max access is write. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend write.
Note 6 (ticket 1), written by Security agent:
  - employment type: contractor
  - security training: basic
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Traci Lowe (E041) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors are never admin; max is read without advanced training. Requested admin exceeds max, so recommend read.
reason: Traci Lowe (E041) requested admin access to Source Code. Five of six notes (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) consistently identify her as a full-time Analyst; only Security claims contractor status. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, and Traci is an Analyst, so she is not the owning role. Per policy, full-time non-owner employees max out at write; admin is not permitted. Since the requested level (admin) exceeds the maximum (write), the maximum is granted.

content.text:
Let me work through this carefully.

The ticket: Traci Lowe (E041) requests admin access to Source Code.

Notes: HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities all say full_time Analyst, recommended write. Security says contractor with basic security training, recommended read.

There's a conflict in the employee facts: most agents say full-time Analyst, but Security says contractor with basic security training.

Hmm. How should the Approver handle conflicting facts? Typically, we need to consider the policy. The policy says full_time employees up to write; admin only if role owns system. Contractor: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Source Code is owned by Engineer role. Traci is Analyst, so she doesn't own it.

If she's full-time: max is write. Requested admin > write, grant write.
If she's contractor with basic training: max is read. Requested admin > read, grant read.

Which to follow? The majority of notes (5 of 6) say full-time Analyst, recommendation write. Security says contractor. There is a discrepancy. I need to make a decision.

The typical approach in these tasks: the majority/ruling evidence determines. HR is usually the authoritative source for employment type. Security's note contradicts. Hmm.

Let me think about which is more reliable. In similar ticket tasks, HR is typically the source of truth for employment facts. Here, 5 agents (HR, IT, Finance, Compliance, Facilities) say full-time Analyst. Only Security says contractor. The security agent's recommendation of read conflicts.

I'll go with the majority: full-time Analyst, max write (since Analyst is not Engineer/owner and admin requires owner). Requested admin is above max write, so grant write.

Let me submit write.
